title: Activities Co-ordinator - Strode Park House
description:
About us

Caring since 1946, Strode Park Foundation provides vital care and support services, supported living opportunities and day and leisure services for young people and adults with a range of disabilities across Kent. Our values of Care, Inspire and Together underpin everything we do, and we are very proud to employ truly inspirational people who make our care settings a remarkable place to work.

About the Role

Join Strode Park House as an Activities Co-ordinator and bring creativity, connection and enjoyment to the lives of the people we support.

Are you energetic, compassionate and full of ideas? Do you believe every day should offer opportunities for fun, friendship and personal achievement? We are looking for an enthusiastic Activities Co-ordinator to create meaningful experiences that help our service users stay active, fulfilled and happy.

In this rewarding role, you will plan and deliver engaging activities, entertainment and outings tailored to each person's interests, choices and care plan. From one-to-one companionship to lively group sessions and community trips, you will make a genuine difference to people's wellbeing, confidence and independence.

This is a full-time, permanent role, working 37.5 hours per week and we are offering an hourly rate of £12.87.

Job Opportunity

What you'll do
- Develop imaginative, person-centred activity programmes with the Therapy & Quality Liaison and Home Management team.
- Lead inclusive social events, activities and outings, ensuring everyone can take part and gain maximum benefit.
- Build warm, respectful relationships with service users and their relatives.
- Support people with personal care, meals, mobility and wellbeing in line with their individual choices and care plans.
- Encourage participation, record outcomes and report changes in wellbeing.
- Drive Foundation transport to support outings and independence.
- Help promote a welcoming, vibrant home through events, including occasional evenings and weekends.

As a Strode Park Foundation colleague you will receive comprehensive support from day one and receive training and development opportunities to develop your skills.

Set within a beautiful 19th-century Victorian manor house surrounded by 14 acres of grounds, Strode Park House offers a relaxed, homely setting for residents on both short- and long-term stays.

Strode Park House is a residential home with nursing care for 55 adults with physical disabilities and complex needs in Herne, Kent. We've been delivering care since 1946, and this residential home is where it all started. For more information, please go to our Strode Park Foundation website.

Company Benefits
- Competitive Rates of Pay
- Paid Disclosure and Barring Service Check
- Employer Pension Contributions
- Free Flu Jab
- Free Parking
- Refer a friend bonus
- Strode Lottery
- Staff Council
- Flexible Hours
- Cycle to Work Scheme
- Staff Newsletter and updates
- Staff Awards

Essential Skills

What you'll bring

You will be creative, enthusiastic, caring and committed to making a difference in adult care. You will communicate clearly, work collaboratively and be comfortable taking direction from the people we support. Flexibility, a full clean driving licence and willingness to drive company vehicles are essential. Experience of disability or supporting disabled people is desirable.

You will also share our commitment to high-quality, safe and person-centred care, confidentiality, professional standards and continuous learning.

description: The postholder will provide an efficient reception service to our patients, doctors and nursing teams. This is a responsible role. Prepare premises punctually in the morning Receive and direct patients, assisting frail, elderly, less mobile patients or any patient as appropriate Answer the telephone courteously and efficiently, taking and recording messages accurately Take requests for appointment bookings and home visits and record these on clinicians lists Make necessary arrangements for repeat prescriptions, blood tests, X Rays and hospital transport Open, sort, process and distribute mail To maintain delegated QOF areas as given by the Operations Lead Receive private fee payments and issue receipts File correspondence, keeping paper medical records in appropriate condition Update computerised records as required Undertake additional administrative tasks as requested Prepare consulting rooms before and after surgery THE MEADS MEDICAL PRACTICE LIMITED JOB DESCRIPTION POSITION: RECEPTIONIST/ADMINISTRATOR REPORTS TO: OPERATIONS LEAD ACCOUNTABLE TO: BUSINESS MANAGER PAY SCALE: Ad Hoc HOURS: By agreement _____________________________________________________________________________ SUMMARY OF RESPONSIBILITIES The post holder will provide an efficient reception service to our patients, doctors and nursing teams. The tasks will include front of house reception, telephone duties and other administrative duties. The work will involve use of telephones, computerised systems including appointments, filing and general surgery assistance. The receptionist is the first point of contact for patients and the general public so it is essential that they present a professional and caring image of the practice and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. This is a responsible role. ____________________________________________________________________________________ MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Reception and Administrative Duties Operate the appointment system as directed; take requests for bookings and home visits and record these on clinicians lists Assemble items for hospital and health authority transport To maintain delegated QOF areas as given by the Operations Manager Lock and secure premises at night as and when directed, checking that the telephone system has transferred correctly to the Out of Hours service Report to the Operations lead any matter affecting patient confidentiality, safety or security. non-judgemental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. title: Clinical Administrator
description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. You will also monitor recalls, screening results and high-risk medication monitoring to help ensure important follow-up is not missed. The role includes supporting QOF, audits, enhanced services and other quality improvement work, alongside patient recall programmes such as immunisations and cervical screening. You will also process insurance and medical reports, monitor the practice email account and provide wider administrative support when required. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential.
